scope: Candidate tooling review for HSWM empirical efficacy, causal identification, and bounded formal verification. No package, model, benchmark, or experiment was installed or run.
method_note: Standard status is not an adoption ranking. Adoption evidence records only a direct publisher, institutional, or scholarly statement. `verified_version` records an observed version or existing HSWM pin; `version_status` says whether that observation was confirmed as an upstream-current release. A tool is a candidate until a task-specific source revision, license, integrity record, isolated qualification, and a HSWM evidence protocol are approved in a separate source-bound plan.
non_substitution_boundary: Agent evaluation measures outcomes under a declared task and resource protocol; causal analysis identifies an estimand only under stated design and assumptions; proof assistants check formal statements; bounded model checking searches finite executions. None establishes the other kind of claim, and none alone establishes HSWM efficacy or FCL passage.

existing_hswm_context.finding: CR-1 through CR-7 remain open; CR-2 requires an explicit assignment, intervention, interference, and identification model, while CR-7 requires a single bounded runtime witness plus independent outcome measurement.
Finite selection, randomized identification, and composition-interference results were machine-checked, but G0 is NOT_PASSED and G1 NOT_EVALUATED.
RU-1 is a candidate; no separately configured calibration API evaluation calls occurred, G0 is NOT_PASSED, and G1 is NOT_EVALUATED.
The checked-in Lean formalization is currently pinned to leanprover/lean4:v4.32.1.
Inspect AI is already integrated as an outer, exact-pinned 0.3.260 preflight observer; it deliberately does not execute HSWM transitions or establish efficacy.
The existing blinded dual-evaluation contract binds Inspector A to inspect-ai==0.3.260 and fail-closes on evaluator disagreement or non-independence.
Existing graph-engineering qualification is RDF/JSON-LD/SHACL/SPARQL-oriented; it does not qualify agent evaluation, causal inference, proof automation, or model checking.

sources.title: Inspect
sources.organization: UK AI Security Institute and Meridian Labs
sources.finding: Inspect documents composable datasets, agents, tools, scorers, sandboxes, over 200 pre-built evaluations, and support for arbitrary external agents.

sources.title: inspect_evals releases
sources.organization: UK Government BEIS / UK AI Security Institute project
sources.finding: The release record documents an inspect_ai >=0.3.258 score-semantics change and warns that it can move reported compliance rates; evaluation versions therefore need source pinning.

sources.title: HSWM Inspect outer preflight
sources.finding: The checked-in observer pins inspect-ai==0.3.260, sanitizes provider-secret inheritance for no-model preflight commands, and explicitly excludes HSWM execution and efficacy claims. This is an HSWM integration pin, not a claim that 0.3.260 is upstream-current.

sources.title: inspect-ai
sources.finding: PyPI lists 0.3.263 as the latest release, uploaded 2026-09-04, and records 0.3.260 as the 2026-08-21 release. HSWM's 0.3.260 pin is therefore observed but is not upstream-current.

sources.title: Releasing AISI's Engineering Playbook
sources.finding: AISI states that Inspect powers many of its frontier evaluations; it reports METR migrated its time-horizon evaluations to Inspect and that Apollo Research builds new evaluations on Inspect. These are AISI-reported adoption statements, not independent comparative measurements.

sources.title: METR Task Standard overview
sources.finding: Defines a common task format with an environment, instructions, and optional automated scoring; METR reports using it for about 200 task families and about 2,000 tasks as of January 2024.

sources.title: METR Example Task Suite
sources.finding: Public tasks conform to METR Task Standard and direct runners to the METR Inspect Task Bridge; publisher labels them work in progress.

sources.title: lm-evaluation-harness releases
sources.finding: Latest listed release v0.4.13 documents fixes that can change results, including few-shot evaluation-document leakage and a multiple-choice filter bug.

sources.title: Lessons from the Trenches on Reproducible Evaluation of Language Models
sources.finding: Describes lm-eval as an independent, reproducible, and extensible evaluation library; this is evidence of intended use, not evidence that any HSWM result generalizes.

sources.title: Lean 4.22.0 release notes
sources.finding: Documents Lean release changes and formal-proof tooling; it is evidence for the proof-assistant ecosystem, not a substitute for reviewing HSWM theorem statements and assumptions.

sources.title: mathlib4
sources.finding: mathlib4 is the community-maintained Lean 4 mathematics and programming library.

sources.title: Mathlib: A Foundation for Formal Mathematics Research and Verification
sources.finding: Lean's official documentation describes Mathlib as enabling research and verification, cites the Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa and Liquid Tensor projects, and describes a human-review process for contributions.

sources.title: LeanDojo-v2
sources.finding: Describes an end-to-end framework for training, evaluating, and deploying AI-assisted Lean 4 theorem provers; its stated installation requires Pantograph for Lean RPC.

sources.title: LeanDojo
sources.finding: The original library labels itself deprecated and directs new projects to LeanDojo-v2; its last listed release is v4.20.0.

sources.title: TLA+ Tools
sources.finding: The toolkit includes a parser, syntax checker, model checker and simulator for an executable subclass, typesetter, and PlusCal translator.

sources.title: Apalache documentation
sources.finding: Apalache is a symbolic TLA+ model checker using SMT solving for finite, bounded executions; its own documentation calls it experimental and describes TLC as mature.

sources.title: DoWhy documentation
sources.finding: DoWhy v0.14 documents explicit identifying assumptions, causal models, effect estimation, refutation, interventions, counterfactuals, and causal graphical models.

sources.title: EconML releases
sources.finding: Latest listed v0.16.0 adds sensitivity analysis for several estimators; the project states its purpose is estimating treatment effects using machine learning.

sources.title: EconML
sources.finding: Microsoft Research describes EconML as open-source causal machine-learning software for individualized causal responses from observational or experimental data.

sources.title: pymc
sources.finding: The PyPI project lists PyMC 6.3.2; it is a probabilistic-programming tool, so posterior uncertainty is conditional on the supplied statistical model.

sources.title: arviz
sources.finding: The PyPI project lists ArviZ 1.3.0; the project describes posterior analysis, model checking, comparison, and diagnostics for Bayesian models.

candidates.name: Inspect AI with Inspect Evals
candidates.standard_status: Open-source evaluation framework, not a formal interoperability standard.
candidates.version_status: Existing HSWM pin; upstream-current version separately observed as 0.3.263 on 2026-09-13. No upgrade is proposed by this review.
candidates.adoption_evidence: AISI reports that Inspect powers many of its frontier evaluations, that METR migrated its time-horizon evaluations to Inspect, and that Apollo Research builds new evaluations on it. These are direct institutional statements, not a popularity ranking or independent effectiveness comparison.
candidates.hswm_fit: Already the HSWM outer evaluator. The immediate CR-1/CR-7 and RU-1 gap is a real held-out evaluator integration: bind frozen baseline, candidate, sham/restore, total-resource accounting, task version, sealed test, and machine-readable traces to the existing observer rather than adding another harness.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: A new harness would duplicate an existing bounded observer. Inspect still cannot define HSWM causal estimands or prove an update rule; model-generated code requires sandbox and log-secret review.
candidates.qualification_needed: Keep the existing 0.3.260 pin; add one source-bound held-out-task integration only after model/provider identity, seed policy, scorer determinism, log custody, and leakage controls are declared. Pin any Inspect Evals task revision separately because upstream scorer changes can move results.

candidates.name: METR Task Standard plus Inspect Task Bridge
candidates.standard_status: Published project specification, explicitly work in progress; not a ratified international standard.
candidates.verified_version: No release/version selected; task definition must declare its standard version.
candidates.version_status: No upstream-current version claim; this review inspected the main specification only.
candidates.adoption_evidence: METR states that it used the format for approximately 200 task families and 2,000 tasks as of January 2024; public tasks state they conform to it.
candidates.hswm_fit: Use after a first HSWM task is stable, to make an outcome task portable beyond a HSWM-only harness and distinguish task construction from agent implementation.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Container/VM environment construction and scorer work are substantial. It overlaps Inspect task execution but adds portability; it does not test continual learning across a task distribution by itself.
candidates.qualification_needed: Choose a task family only after the estimand and source cutoff are fixed; pin the standard revision, image digest, external-service policy, scorer tests, and bridge revision; verify no HSWM state crosses reset boundaries.

candidates.name: lm-evaluation-harness
candidates.version_status: Observed as the latest listed release on 2026-09-13.
candidates.adoption_evidence: The authors describe the project as an independent, reproducible, extensible evaluation library; this does not establish suitability for HSWM's agentic causal claims.
candidates.hswm_fit: Useful only as a fixed-model regression and contamination-sensitive language baseline. It can establish that a model/API change shifts static task scores before running a dynamic HSWM protocol.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Directly overlaps only static benchmark scoring. Its release notes show score-affecting leakage fixes, so historical scores cannot be compared across versions without a migration record.
candidates.qualification_needed: Pin harness, task YAML, dataset revision, tokenizer/template, decoding parameters, model revision, and scoring patch level; require held-out task suitability review and no use as a proxy for causal learning.

candidates.name: Lean 4 and mathlib
candidates.standard_status: Proof assistant and community library, not a graph or experiment standard.
candidates.verified_version: HSWM checked-in pin: leanprover/lean4:v4.32.1; no upgrade selected.
candidates.version_status: Existing HSWM pin, not an upstream-current version claim.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Lean's official Mathlib use-case documentation cites frontier formalization projects and describes a reviewed common library; existing HSWM proof artifacts already use Lean. This does not validate HSWM theorem premises.
candidates.hswm_fit: Keep as the primary formal layer for CR-0 through CR-6: formalize the finite randomized assignment/identification model, noninterference prerequisites, and composition preservation before claiming a constructed witness.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Already present and avoids duplicate formal stacks. It cannot validate that runtime traces faithfully represent reality or that the stated environment assumptions hold.
candidates.qualification_needed: Retain the local toolchain pin and build with trust restrictions; for each theorem record exact statement, imports, admitted axioms, `sorry` audit, and the empirical mapping that remains outside Lean.

candidates.name: LeanDojo-v2 with Pantograph
candidates.category: AI-assisted theorem-prover training/evaluation and Lean RPC
candidates.standard_status: Research/project tooling, not a proof checker or standard.
candidates.verified_version: LeanDojo-v2 main documentation reviewed; exact immutable revision not selected.
candidates.version_status: No upstream-current version claim; the original LeanDojo repository labels itself deprecated in favor of v2.
candidates.adoption_evidence: The project explicitly supersedes its original deprecated library with LeanDojo-v2; no broad-adoption inference is made from this source review.
candidates.hswm_fit: Potential future instrument for measuring an LLM-assisted proof-search policy on HSWM-local lemmas, separately from accepting proofs. It could support bounded research on whether outcome feedback improves proof search.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Adds Python, Lean RPC, model, GPU/dataset, and GitHub-token dependencies; it overlaps existing direct Lean checking but does not replace its kernel.
candidates.qualification_needed: Do not add until a preregistered theorem-search study exists. Then pin LeanDojo-v2, Pantograph, Lean/mathlib, theorem corpus cutoff, model, prompt, retry/budget policy, and held-out theorem split; report accepted kernel proofs separately from search success.

candidates.name: TLA+ Tools and TLC
candidates.standard_status: Established specification-language/tool ecosystem; no claim of formal standards-body ratification.
candidates.verified_version: No exact version selected in this review.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Microsoft distributes the toolkit and documents the parser, model checker, simulator, and PlusCal translator; no popularity ranking is inferred.
candidates.hswm_fit: Strong candidate for a small finite CR-0/CR-6 protocol model: concurrent revision proposals, owner/Permit transition ordering, migration, conflict resolution, and rollback/recovery safety invariants.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Complements Lean: TLC finds counterexample traces in bounded instances; it does not prove unbounded theorems or establish probabilistic/effect-size claims. A translation must not become a second HSWM runtime.
candidates.qualification_needed: Write a source-bound finite abstraction with explicit abstraction loss, state bounds, invariants, fairness assumptions, and reproducible TLC configuration; independently relate any discovered trace to the TypeScript Effect transition semantics.

candidates.name: Apalache
candidates.verified_version: No exact version selected in this review.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Its official documentation calls it a symbolic TLA+ checker and explicitly identifies it as experimental; no broader adoption claim is made.
candidates.hswm_fit: Use only if the TLC state space blocks the CR-0/CR-6 finite abstraction and an SMT-based bounded search gives a concrete advantage.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Overlaps TLC's finite model-checking purpose, adds SMT solver/version sensitivity, and remains bounded by documented finite parameter/execution assumptions.
candidates.qualification_needed: Compare one identical finite specification against TLC first; pin Apalache and solver versions, config, bounds, and counterexample replay. Reject it if it adds no falsification reach beyond TLC.

candidates.name: DoWhy
candidates.category: causal identification, estimation, refutation, intervention/counterfactual analysis
candidates.standard_status: Open-source causal-inference library, not a causal-identification standard.
candidates.version_status: Observed in the current documentation; no independent latest-release assertion is made.
candidates.adoption_evidence: PyWhy's documentation states that identifying assumptions are first-class and publishes the v0.14 API; this is direct project evidence only.
candidates.hswm_fit: Highest-priority causal-analysis candidate for CR-2 once an HSWM experiment declares treatment/revision, outcome, unit, interference boundary, DAG, and refuters. It forces the identification assumptions into the recorded protocol.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Overlaps parts of custom analysis but adds explicit causal-model and refutation discipline. It cannot repair violated randomization, hidden interference, outcome leakage, or a post-hoc estimand.
candidates.qualification_needed: Create a synthetic randomized HSWM-like data-generating process with known estimand; pin library/graph algorithms; confirm the DAG, treatment timing, unit, SUTVA/interference policy, identification output, placebo/subset/unobserved-confounding refuters, and calculation against an independent implementation.

candidates.name: EconML
candidates.standard_status: Open-source research library, not a standard.
candidates.version_status: Observed as the latest listed release on 2026-09-13.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Microsoft Research identifies EconML as its ALICE project's open-source software; the release record documents sensitivity analysis in v0.16.0.
candidates.hswm_fit: A second-stage CR-2/CR-3 tool when the effect may differ by task family, scale, topology, or cell/coalition context and sample size supports a prespecified heterogeneous-effect analysis.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Partly overlaps DoWhy estimators and is conditional on the same causal assumptions. Flexible CATE estimates can magnify multiple-testing and low-power risks in the current small-data state.
candidates.qualification_needed: Use only after DoWhy identifies the estimand and a power plan supports heterogeneity. Pin estimator/nuisance models/cross-fitting/random seed; preregister effect modifiers and sensitivity analysis; compare against a simple randomized paired estimator.

candidates.name: PyMC with ArviZ
candidates.category: Bayesian outcome modeling, diagnostics, and posterior predictive checking
candidates.standard_status: Open-source probabilistic-programming and analysis ecosystem, not a standard.
candidates.version_status: Observed as current PyPI releases on 2026-09-13.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Package publishers document current releases and ArviZ's posterior analysis/model-checking role; no popularity ranking is inferred.
candidates.hswm_fit: Useful for a planned multi-level repeated-task analysis: uncertainty intervals, partial pooling across task families/scales, posterior predictive checks, and sensitivity to a declared observation model.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Complements frequentist randomization analysis and DoWhy; posterior results depend on likelihood, priors, and hierarchy. It cannot identify a causal effect without the experimental design/assumptions.
candidates.qualification_needed: Defer until sufficient repeated outcomes exist. Then preregister model, priors, diagnostics thresholds, posterior predictive checks, code/data hashes, and a parallel randomization/frequentist analysis; do not use a favorable posterior model as a substitute for a causal design.
